title: Failure to Drop Elevated Privileges Post-Startup
pattern: Starting an application with elevated operating system privileges (such as Unix `root`) to perform initial bootstrap operations (like binding to port 80), but failing to permanently drop those privileges before handling untrusted requests.
why_bad: If an application continues to run as root, any subsequent code execution or buffer overflow vulnerability in request handlers immediately grants the attacker full root access to the entire server container.
detection: The application startup code binding sockets or reading master files as root but lacking execution steps that invoke system calls (`setuid`, `setgid`) to drop status.
fix: Employ privilege separation: execute the initial startup bindings as root, then invoke standard system calls to permanently downgrade process privilege level to an unprivileged user before processing data.
source: `Michael T. Nygard - Release It! (2007)`, Ch 12, p. 272-273; `Heather Adkins et al. (2020)`, Ch 5, p. 78.
